subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix this first as default viewport anchoring/renderer behavior, or should OpenClaw add a user-facing TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the issue crosses terminal UX policy and pi-tui renderer behavior; adding a preference would create new product/config surface while a default anchor fix may solve the reported disruption without one.

options.title: Repair default anchoring first
options.body: Fix the TUI/renderer path so it preserves reading position and only auto-follows when already at the bottom, with live or PTY proof before merge.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose an explicit TUI mode or command, accepting the extra product/config surface and upgrade documentation burden.

options.title: Fold into renderer scrollback work
options.body: Treat the narrower open renderer/scrollback issue as the implementation owner and keep this issue as user-facing validation context.

recommendation.title: Repair default anchoring first
recommendation.body: Fix the TUI/renderer path so it preserves reading position and only auto-follows when already at the bottom, with live or PTY proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent TUI refresh work plus merge history on adjacent TUI fixes make this the best available product-direction owner from the inspected history.
